runtime_provenance.prior_docstring:
Declare native input in batches of up to 2,048 rows and 128 fields.

    Each batch is a sequence of row mappings. Schema is explicit and admits
    nullable int64, finite float64, bool and utf8. Input is pulled at execution;
    pass a factory for repeated calls, or an iterable for one execution. Total
    input is limited to 4,096 batches. The default resident mode retains all
    native input under the query memory grant. ``streaming=True`` instead
    admits one source used once through pure filters/projections, incremental
    results, a bounded small collection or one native Vortex output. Other
    operators require explicit resident mode. Results remain provisional until
    the producer ends and final validation succeeds.

page.main:
Python

Use Python to read local data, build queries, and inspect or export results. Admitted queries run in ShardLoom. Unsupported work returns a diagnostic without fallback execution.

Run a local query
Section titled “Run a local query”

Create the small CSV in the getting-started walkthrough before running this example. The public run() report exposes the result and native execution evidence.

import shardloom as sl


ctx = sl.context()
result = (
    ctx.read("data/orders.csv")
       .filter(sl.col("status") == "paid")
       .limit(10)
       .run()
)


print(result.envelope.field_int("output_row_count"))
print(result.envelope.human_text)
print(result.fallback_attempted, result.external_engine_invoked)

ctx.read(path) infers local adapters for .csv, .json, .jsonl, .ndjson, .parquet, .arrow, .ipc, .feather, .avro, .orc, and .vortex. CSV, flat JSON/JSONL/NDJSON, generated rows, and scoped local Vortex inputs are the default public examples. Parquet, Arrow IPC/Feather, Avro, and ORC are scoped local-format surfaces when the matching feature-gated build is present; otherwise ShardLoom returns deterministic adapter blockers without fallback execution.

Reuse And Export
Section titled “Reuse And Export”

Python contexts can retain a local worker to avoid per-call CLI startup. Automatic preparation reuses an unchanged source only when its schema and artifact identities match. Each query still has fresh execution state; a prepared artifact is not a cache of query results.

Admitted flat results can use write_vortex, write_parquet, write_arrow_ipc, write_avro, write_orc, write_csv, write_json, and write_jsonl through the shared native result and sink contracts. Feature gates, supported types, and result limits apply. See runtime and I/O and the user-surface index.

Consume results in batches
Section titled “Consume results in batches”

Current source builds add iter_batches() for admitted results and from_batches() for explicitly typed resident input. These additions merged in PR #1526 after complete local and hosted checks; published v0.4.0 packages predate them. Source builds also admit opt-in streaming=True for one finite source used once through scan/filter/project, global sorting, aggregation and limits. See the scope and local acceptance.

def orders():
    yield [{"order_id": 1, "amount": 12.5}]
    yield [{"order_id": 2, "amount": None}]


frame = sl.from_batches(
    orders, schema={"order_id": "int64", "amount": "float64"},
    streaming=True,
)
with frame.iter_batches(batch_rows=1024) as batches:
    for batch in batches:
        print(batch.result_rows)
    assert batches.report is not None

Input admits nullable Int64, finite Float64, booleans and UTF8 strings with an explicit schema. Each input batch contains at most 2,048 row mappings and an 8 MiB frame, with up to 128 fields and 4,096 batches per source. In the default resident mode (streaming=False), total native input must fit the query memory grant. A factory, as above, supplies fresh input for repeated calls; an iterable can be consumed once.

Streaming retains at most one native input batch, so cumulative input may exceed the query grant within those finite limits. It supports incremental results, bounded small collection or one native Vortex destination. Retained operator state shares the grant; ordering and general aggregation support an explicit native spill policy. Limits and offsets drain and validate the complete source, including zero limits. Joins, repeated sources, sets, windows and dynamic schemas reject before producer consumption. The producer must reach its explicit end event before results are final. Typed intake and output compaction are charged copies; output and sink reservations remain separate. No repeated-source spool or process-RSS ceiling is added. See the streamed ordering contract and aggregate spill example.

Requesting the next result batch acknowledges the preceding one. Use the context manager when stopping early, and treat delivered batches as provisional until the final report is present after full exhaustion. Prepare compatibility file inputs explicitly to Vortex before batch consumption. See resource boundaries.

Next steps
Section titled “Next steps”

See the examples for preparation, bounded collection, writes, and blocker inspection. The limitations page describes current coverage gaps.

Native aggregation and streamed ordering acceptance

Status: complete local engine acceptance and independent portable-packet inspection pass for runtime 8a207745a55fb5678cd2b56866effb6fb0eb9352. Affected support pages, native examples and local browser checks also pass; hosted integration remains pending. Published v0.4.0 is unchanged; this finite capability does not close the remaining local workflow scope.

Accepted behavior

One finite, single-use streaming=True source now executes through the complete shared Scan/Filter/Project/Sort/Limit/Aggregate tree. Global limits and offsets drain and validate the producer, including zero limits. Retaining operators and delivered results own credited native payload independently of the input batch. Incremental results, bounded collection and one new Vortex destination preserve the existing completion and publication contract.

An explicit spill policy admits general relational aggregation through the existing stable native ordering, run store and exact scalar reducers. Grouping and COUNT DISTINCT no longer require a resident entry per distinct key/value under that strategy. First-seen group order, null behavior, logical types and ordered floating reductions remain intact. Without the policy, the resident strategy and deterministic memory denial remain available. All nested stages share the same memory grant and spill quota.

The ordering design, aggregate design and public spill example describe admission, reuse, ownership and failures. File-backed aggregates retain all eight admitted writers; this does not admit compatibility writers for streamed batch input. There is no external query-engine execution.

Constrained-state proof

Both aggregate cases consume 133,137 rows and 70,330,932 original logical input bytes, exceeding four times the 16 MiB native grant. The constrained resident control denies; the native spill strategy and separate 256 MiB resident control complete and compare every output value. The preserved focused observations are:

Native case	Complete output rows	Spill peak reserved bytes	Runs / merges	Peak disk bytes
High-cardinality groups	133,137	9,090,433	676 / 337	289,792,624
One group with high-cardinality DISTINCT	1	9,257,041	259 / 129	158,249,316

Both verify quota enforcement, completed owned cleanup and return to the reservation baseline. The final full native suite reruns the identical pressure-test sources; the table's counters come from the retained focused run. Streamed ordering separately completes 66,567 rows whose logical input exceeds four times its 8 MiB native grant, with resident denial, a 128 MiB ample control, multiple real spill merges and every output value checked.

The file-backed eight-writer aggregate proof uses a 64 MiB grant to accommodate its reader/writer overlap. Its earlier smaller-grant denial is preserved. Public streaming cases use a separate 1 GiB grant and do not establish a larger-than-grant result. Native reservations are not process RSS, and this unit does not claim complete coverage of all provider allocations.

Complete workflow and regression proof
Check	Result
Public finite streaming suite	109 cases; 94 raw envelopes, 61 small-value files and ten malformed protocol traces reopened
Saved public pressure output	All 248,846 rows reopened and independently reconstructed across eight resident/spill/write captures
Existing public relational portfolio	27,373 cases and 15,820,181 complete row comparisons across five materializations; all 54,733 raw envelopes reopened
Direct unary portfolio	202 cases and 131,734 complete rows; 367 raw envelopes reopened
Resident batch adapters / format fidelity	48 / 19 checks, including independent compatibility-format readback
Admitted semantics / golden workflows	145 / 9 stages
Retained full dataset	All 43 queries run three times; every complete result matches the preexisting reference
Source and build gates	Fourteen gates pass, including required workspace format/lint/tests, native CLI/Vortex tests and lint, examples, feature-light and MSRV checks, and 615 Python tests

Native and public tests cover empty/null/typed/nested groups and values, COUNT/COUNT DISTINCT/SUM/AVG/MIN/MAX, alias sharing, first-seen order, cross-batch distinct values, nested aggregate/order/limit composition, input release and retained output. Failures cover late producer/schema/value errors, zero limits, cancellation, exhausted grants/quota, actual corrupt runs, failed consumers, source mutation, publication and verified abandoned-run cleanup. Unknown files remain protected. Cleanup and restart are proven; execution resume and automatic recovery of crashed output staging are not claimed.

Required workspace commands pass with the frozen implementation:

cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --all-targets

The packet retains exact offline/locked commands and every gate receipt. After an obsolete CLI test expected explicit streaming limits to be denied, the test was corrected to verify complete drain and late failures. Only that CLI test file changed between the two gate attempts. Four unaffected gates were reused with exact asset and feature-gating proof; all CLI checks and subsequent gates passed on the corrected source. No dependency audit rerun is claimed: all 23 manifest, lockfile and vendored assets match the prior accepted build.

The full-dataset observation uses the unchanged, fully resident 15,682,956,489-byte Vortex artifact, 24 GiB policy and maximum parallelism 12. The sum of per-query minima is 70.113672 seconds, medians 71.381934 seconds and all 129 calls 216.147038 seconds. These are complete-process correctness observations with uncontrolled ordinary host activity and a prehashed source; they support no comparative speedup or RSS enforcement claim. An earlier long host-observation gap during the public regression is retained separately and is not represented as uninterrupted timing evidence.

Full43 preflight initially refused accumulated log storage before queries. The 516 call artifacts from one completed historical cohort were archived and verified before removing redundant originals, recovering 3,362,816 accounted bytes. Failed/incomplete observations and storage limits were unchanged. Fresh preflight and Full43 then passed. Finalization independently reopened all 516 archive members; original development failures and corrections remain recorded.

"""Bind hosted acceptance to the locally accepted stateful implementation."""
import argparse
from datetime import datetime, timezone
import json
import subprocess

import stateful_support_common as support

c = support.c
HEAD = 'a1f7268c726d80d154e5d4e310a291c3f65e209e'
BASE = 'c16f8da71581c1b1b874aaa18aefa95a8264d0ad'
RUNTIME = '8a207745a55fb5678cd2b56866effb6fb0eb9352'
PREVIEW = 'https://c36e5896-shardloom.djheinrich.workers.dev'
REPORT = 'docs/benchmarks/native-stateful-aggregation-ordering-2026-10-08.md'
GH = '/opt/homebrew/bin/gh'
REPO = 'depsilon/shardloom'


def run(*command):
    return subprocess.check_output(command, cwd=c.ROOT, text=True, timeout=60).strip()


def pr(number):
    return json.loads(run(GH, 'pr', 'view', str(number), '--repo', REPO, '--json',
        'number,url,state,isDraft,headRefOid,baseRefOid,mergeCommit,mergedAt,mergeStateStatus,statusCheckRollup,reviews,comments'))


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--stage', choices=('premerge', 'postmerge'), required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--attempt', type=int, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    assert args.attempt > 0
    prefix = f'stateful-hosted-{args.stage}-{args.attempt}'
    observed, baseline = pr(1531), pr(1530)
    query = '''query { repository(owner: "depsilon", name: "shardloom") {
      pullRequest(number: 1531) {
        reviewThreads(first: 100) { nodes { id isResolved isOutdated
          comments(first: 100) { nodes { body url author { login } }
            pageInfo { hasNextPage } } } pageInfo { hasNextPage } }
        reviews(last: 100) { nodes { state body submittedAt commit { oid } author { login } }
          pageInfo { hasPreviousPage } }
        comments(last: 100) { nodes { id body url author { login } }
          pageInfo { hasPreviousPage } }
      }
    } }'''
    reviews = json.loads(run(GH, 'api', 'graphql', '-f', 'query=' + query))
    runs = json.loads(run(GH, 'api', 'repos/' + REPO
        + '/actions/runs?event=pull_request&head_sha=' + HEAD + '&per_page=100'))
    snapshot = {'pr': observed, 'baseline_pr': baseline, 'reviews': reviews,
        'workflow_runs': runs, 'observed_at': datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}
    c.write(c.OUT / (prefix + '-snapshot.json'), snapshot)
    assert not c.git('status', '--porcelain'), 'requires the clean accepted tree'
    assert observed['headRefOid'] == HEAD and not observed['isDraft']
    assert baseline['state'] == 'MERGED' and baseline['mergeCommit']['oid'] == BASE
    expected = {row['name'] for row in baseline['statusCheckRollup']}
    assert len(expected) == 39
    for workflow in ('.github/workflows/ci.yml', '.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml'):
        assert c.git('show', BASE + ':' + workflow) == c.git('show', HEAD + ':' + workflow)
    checks = observed['statusCheckRollup']
    assert len(checks) == len(expected) and {row['name'] for row in checks} == expected
    assert all(row['status'] == 'COMPLETED' and row['conclusion'] == 'SUCCESS'
        for row in checks), [(row['name'], row['status'], row['conclusion'])
                            for row in checks if row['conclusion'] != 'SUCCESS']
    assert runs['total_count'] == len(runs['workflow_runs']) == 2
    assert {row['name'] for row in runs['workflow_runs']} == {'CI', 'CodeQL Analysis'}
    assert all(row['head_sha'] == HEAD and row['status'] == 'completed'
        and row['conclusion'] == 'success' for row in runs['workflow_runs'])
    assert 'errors' not in reviews
    review = reviews['data']['repository']['pullRequest']
    assert not review['reviewThreads']['pageInfo']['hasNextPage']
    assert not review['reviews']['pageInfo']['hasPreviousPage']
    assert not review['comments']['pageInfo']['hasPreviousPage']
    assert not review['reviewThreads']['nodes'], 'new threads require primary inspection'
    assert not review['reviews']['nodes'], 'new reviews require primary inspection'
    summaries = [row for row in review['comments']['nodes']
        if row['author']['login'] == 'chatgpt-codex-connector'
        and '<!-- codex-pull-request-review-summary -->' in row['body']]
    assert len(summaries) == 1
    lines = [line for line in summaries[0]['body'].splitlines() if '**Code Review**' in line]
    assert len(lines) == 1 and '✅ **Completed**' in lines[0] and f'`{HEAD[:7]}`' in lines[0]
    assert len(review['comments']['nodes']) == 2, 'new comments require primary inspection'
    assert any(row['author']['login'] == 'cloudflare-workers-and-pages'
        and 'Deployment successful!' in row['body']
        and PREVIEW in row['body'] and HEAD[:8] in row['body']
        for row in review['comments']['nodes'])

    source, build, annotation = support.checked_runtime()
    assert source['head'] == RUNTIME and len(source['source_hashes']) == 964
    assert annotation['assets_byte_identical'] == 963
    assert annotation['entire_module_ast_identical_after_replacing_only_named_docstring']
    assert not annotation['executable_behavior_changed']
    acceptance = c.read(c.OUT / 'stateful-final-acceptance-1.json')
    assert acceptance['status'] == 'passed_local_engine'
    assert acceptance['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert c.sha(build['binary']) == build['binary_sha256'] == acceptance['binary_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.OUT / acceptance['packet']) == acceptance['packet_sha256']
    index = c.read(c.ROOT / 'docs/benchmarks/evidence/native-stateful-aggregation-ordering-2026-10-08.json')
    assert index['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME
    assert index['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert index['acceptance']['packet_sha256'] == acceptance['packet_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['acceptance']['packet']) == acceptance['packet_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['portable_inspection']) == index['portable_inspection_sha256']
    assert index['support_alignment_runtime_provenance'] == annotation
    assert index['documentation_updates_complete'] and not index['hosted_acceptance_complete']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance']) == index['documentation_acceptance_sha256']
    docs = c.read(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance'])
    assert docs['status'] == 'passed_local_documentation_acceptance'
    assert docs['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME and docs['runtime_provenance'] == annotation
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / docs['archive']['path']) == docs['archive']['sha256']
    assert docs['archive']['all_members_reopened_and_hash_checked']
    for name, identity in docs['source_files'].items():
        path = c.ROOT / name
        assert path.stat().st_size == identity['bytes'] and c.sha(path) == identity['sha256'], name
    preview_path = c.OUT / 'stateful-hosted-preview-1.json'
    preview = c.read(preview_path)
    assert preview['status'] == 'passed_hosted_search_and_guide' and preview['head'] == HEAD
    assert preview['preview'] == PREVIEW and preview['resultCount'] == 4
    assert preview['search'] == 'aggregation' and preview['tabClosed']
    assert preview['landedUrl'] == PREVIEW + '/field-guide/python-surface/#consume-results-in-batches'
    assert preview['page']['url'] == preview['landedUrl']
    assert preview['page']['body'] <= preview['page']['viewport'] and not preview['console']
    assert preview['page']['acceptanceLinks'] == ['https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/' + REPORT]
    assert 'global sorting, aggregation and limits' in preview['page']['main']
    assert 'Limits and offsets drain and validate the complete source, including zero limits.' in preview['page']['main']
    assert not index['broader_resource_spill_recovery_complete']
    assert not index['package_publication_performed'] and not index['performance_claim_allowed']
    if args.stage == 'premerge':
        assert observed['state'] == 'OPEN' and observed['mergeStateStatus'] == 'CLEAN'
        assert observed['baseRefOid'] == BASE and c.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == HEAD
        assert c.git('ls-remote', '--heads', 'origin', 'main').split()[0] == BASE
        merge = None
    else:
        assert observed['state'] == 'MERGED' and observed['mergedAt']
        merge = observed['mergeCommit']['oid']
        assert c.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == merge
        assert c.git('rev-list', '--parents', '-n', '1', merge).split() == [merge, BASE, HEAD]
        assert c.git('rev-parse', merge + '^{tree}') == c.git('rev-parse', HEAD + '^{tree}')
        assert c.git('ls-remote', '--heads', 'origin', 'main').split()[0] == merge
    result = {
        'status': 'passed_' + args.stage, 'pr': 1531, 'head': HEAD, 'base': BASE,
        'baseline_pr': 1530, 'merge_commit': merge,
        'successful_hosted_checks': len(checks), 'hosted_check_names': sorted(expected),
        'runtime_commit': RUNTIME, 'runtime_provenance': annotation,
        'source_identity_sha256': source['source_identity_sha256'],
        'runtime_binary_sha256': acceptance['binary_sha256'],
        'acceptance_packet_sha256': acceptance['packet_sha256'],
        'documentation_archive_sha256': docs['archive']['sha256'],
        'hosted_preview_search_passed': True, 'hosted_preview_browser_sha256': c.sha(preview_path),
        'snapshot_sha256': c.sha(c.OUT / (prefix + '-snapshot.json')),
        'local_engine_acceptance_sha256': c.sha(c.OUT / 'stateful-final-acceptance-1.json'),
        'observed_preview_url': PREVIEW,
        'review_state': 'no_new_submitted_reviews_or_threads_observed',
        'hosted_automated_review': 'completed_no_posted_findings',
        'submitted_approval_inferred': False, 'broader_roadmap_complete': False,
        'package_publication_attempted': False, 'driver_sha256': c.sha(__file__),
    }
    c.write(c.OUT / (prefix + '.json'), result)
    print(json.dumps({key: result[key] for key in ('status', 'head', 'merge_commit',
        'successful_hosted_checks', 'hosted_automated_review')}, indent=2), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import hashlib
import json
import subprocess

import stateful_support_common as support
from verify_stateful_hosted import BASE, GH, HEAD, PREVIEW, REPO, REPORT, RUNTIME

c = support.c
EVIDENCE = c.ROOT / 'docs/benchmarks/evidence'


def main():
    pre = c.read(c.OUT / 'stateful-hosted-premerge-1.json')
    post = c.read(c.OUT / 'stateful-hosted-postmerge-1.json')
    assert pre['status'] == 'passed_premerge' and post['status'] == 'passed_postmerge'
    assert pre['head'] == post['head'] == HEAD and pre['base'] == post['base'] == BASE
    assert pre['baseline_pr'] == post['baseline_pr'] == 1530
    assert pre['successful_hosted_checks'] == post['successful_hosted_checks'] == 39
    assert pre['hosted_check_names'] == post['hosted_check_names']
    assert pre['hosted_automated_review'] == post['hosted_automated_review'] == 'completed_no_posted_findings'
    assert not pre['submitted_approval_inferred'] and not post['submitted_approval_inferred']
    merge = post['merge_commit']
    assert c.git('rev-parse', 'HEAD') == merge and not c.git('status', '--porcelain')
    assert c.git('rev-list', '--parents', '-n', '1', merge).split() == [merge, BASE, HEAD]
    assert c.git('rev-parse', HEAD + '^{tree}') == c.git('rev-parse', merge + '^{tree}')
    source, build, annotation = support.checked_runtime()
    assert pre['runtime_commit'] == post['runtime_commit'] == source['head'] == RUNTIME
    assert pre['runtime_provenance'] == post['runtime_provenance'] == annotation
    assert len(source['source_hashes']) == 964 and annotation['assets_byte_identical'] == 963
    acceptance = c.read(c.OUT / 'stateful-final-acceptance-1.json')
    assert acceptance['status'] == 'passed_local_engine'
    assert pre['source_identity_sha256'] == post['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert c.sha(build['binary']) == build['binary_sha256'] == acceptance['binary_sha256']
    assert pre['runtime_binary_sha256'] == post['runtime_binary_sha256'] == acceptance['binary_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.OUT / acceptance['packet']) == acceptance['packet_sha256']
    for stage, record in (('premerge', pre), ('postmerge', post)):
        assert c.sha(c.OUT / f'stateful-hosted-{stage}-1-snapshot.json') == record['snapshot_sha256']
        guard = c.read(c.OUT / f'stateful-hosted-{stage}-check-1.json')
        assert guard['status'] == 'passed' and guard['returncode'] == 0 and guard['process_group_drained']
        assert guard['log_sha256'] == c.sha(c.OUT / f'stateful-hosted-{stage}-check-1.log')
    index = c.read(EVIDENCE / 'native-stateful-aggregation-ordering-2026-10-08.json')
    assert index['runtime_commit'] == RUNTIME and index['support_alignment_runtime_provenance'] == annotation
    assert index['source_identity_sha256'] == source['source_identity_sha256']
    assert index['documentation_updates_complete'] and not index['hosted_acceptance_complete']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['acceptance']['packet']) == index['acceptance']['packet_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['portable_inspection']) == index['portable_inspection_sha256']
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance']) == index['documentation_acceptance_sha256']
    docs = c.read(c.ROOT / index['documentation_acceptance'])
    assert c.sha(c.ROOT / docs['archive']['path']) == docs['archive']['sha256']
    assert pre['documentation_archive_sha256'] == post['documentation_archive_sha256'] == docs['archive']['sha256']
    for name, identity in docs['source_files'].items():
        assert (c.ROOT / name).stat().st_size == identity['bytes'] and c.sha(c.ROOT / name) == identity['sha256'], name
    assert not index['broader_resource_spill_recovery_complete']
    assert not index['package_publication_performed'] and not index['performance_claim_allowed']

    preview_path = c.OUT / 'stateful-hosted-preview-1.json'
    preview = c.read(preview_path)
    production = c.read(c.OUT / 'stateful-hosted-production-1.json')
    link = c.read(c.OUT / 'stateful-hosted-production-link-1.json')
    assert preview['head'] == HEAD and preview['preview'] == PREVIEW
    assert pre['hosted_preview_browser_sha256'] == post['hosted_preview_browser_sha256'] == c.sha(preview_path)
    assert production['merge_commit'] == merge and production['origin'] == 'https://shardloom.io'
    for origin, page in ((PREVIEW, preview), ('https://shardloom.io', production)):
        assert page['status'] == 'passed_hosted_search_and_guide'
        assert page['page']['url'] == origin + '/field-guide/python-surface/#consume-results-in-batches'
        assert page['landedUrl'] == page['page']['url']
        assert page['page']['body'] <= page['page']['viewport']
        assert page['search'] == 'aggregation' and page['resultCount'] == 4 and page['tabClosed']
        assert not page['console']
        assert page['page']['acceptanceLinks'] == ['https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/blob/main/' + REPORT]
    assert preview['page']['main'] == production['page']['main']
    assert link['url'] == production['page']['acceptanceLinks'][0]
    assert link['status'] == 'passed_merged_report_link' and link['tabClosed']
    assert '27,373' in link['body'] and '129' in link['body']
    report_bytes = subprocess.check_output([GH, 'api', 'repos/' + REPO + '/contents/' + REPORT,
        '-f', 'ref=' + merge, '-X', 'GET', '-H', 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json'],
        cwd=c.ROOT, timeout=45)
    assert report_bytes == (c.ROOT / REPORT).read_bytes()
    assert RUNTIME in report_bytes.decode()
    checks = json.loads(subprocess.check_output([GH, 'api', 'repos/' + REPO + '/commits/' + merge
        + '/check-runs?per_page=100'], cwd=c.ROOT, text=True, timeout=45))
    deployments = [row for row in checks['check_runs'] if row['name'] == 'Workers Builds: shardloom']
    assert len(deployments) == 1
    deployment = deployments[0]
    assert deployment['head_sha'] == merge and deployment['status'] == 'completed'
    assert deployment['conclusion'] == 'success'
    c.write(c.OUT / 'stateful-production-deployment-1.json', deployment)
    names = [
        'stateful-hosted-premerge-1.json', 'stateful-hosted-premerge-1-snapshot.json',
        'stateful-hosted-postmerge-1.json', 'stateful-hosted-postmerge-1-snapshot.json',
        'stateful-hosted-premerge-check-1.json', 'stateful-hosted-premerge-check-1.log',
        'stateful-hosted-postmerge-check-1.json', 'stateful-hosted-postmerge-check-1.log',
        'stateful-hosted-preview-1.json', 'stateful-hosted-production-1.json',
        'stateful-hosted-production-link-1.json', 'stateful-production-deployment-1.json',
        'verify_stateful_hosted.py', 'build_stateful_hosted_receipt.py', 'stateful_support_common.py',
    ]
    records = []
    for name in names:
        data = (c.OUT / name).read_bytes()
        records.append({'name': name, 'bytes': len(data), 'sha256': hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest(),
            'contents': json.loads(data) if name.endswith('.json') else data.decode()})
    images = []
    for surface, page in (('preview', preview), ('production', production)):
        for number, name in enumerate(page['screenshots'], 1):
            original = c.OUT / name
            target = EVIDENCE / f'native-stateful-{surface}-{number}-2026-10-08.png'
            with target.open('xb') as stream:
                stream.write(original.read_bytes())
            assert c.sha(original) == c.sha(target)
            images.append({'path': target.name, 'bytes': target.stat().st_size, 'sha256': c.sha(target)})
    record = {
        'schema_version': 'shardloom.native_stateful_hosted_acceptance.v1',
        'status': 'passed_hosted_integration', 'pr_url': 'https://github.com/depsilon/shardloom/pull/1531',
        'head': HEAD, 'merge_commit': merge, 'successful_pr_checks': 39,
        'merge_tree_equals_accepted_head': True, 'runtime_commit': RUNTIME,
        'runtime_provenance': annotation, 'source_identity_sha256': source['source_identity_sha256'],
        'runtime_binary_sha256': acceptance['binary_sha256'],
        'review': 'Primary review and complete local acceptance preceded merge. Automated review completed for the accepted head with no posted findings. No submitted approval is inferred.',
        'website': 'Preview and merged production search returned four results and opened the batch guide without console warnings or errors. Complete rendered guide text matches; its acceptance link opens the merged report. Exact report bytes match accepted source. Historical hosted-pending status in the original local acceptance records is preserved.',
        'report_identity': {'path': REPORT, 'commit': merge, 'bytes': len(report_bytes),
            'sha256': hashlib.sha256(report_bytes).hexdigest()},
        'temporary_tabs_closed': True, 'package_publication_attempted': False,
        'broader_resource_spill_recovery_complete': False,
        'process_rss_cap_claim': False, 'broad_engine_speedup_claim': False,
        'records': records, 'images': images,
    }
    serialized = support.portable(record)
    assert '/' + 'Users' + '/' not in serialized and '/' + 'home' + '/' not in serialized
    target = EVIDENCE / 'native-stateful-hosted-2026-10-08.json'
    with target.open('x') as stream:
        stream.write(serialized)
    assert c.read(target) == json.loads(serialized)
    print(json.dumps({'status': record['status'], 'sha256': c.sha(target),
        'bytes': target.stat().st_size, 'records': len(records), 'images': len(images)}), flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':

"""Verify the accepted runtime plus exactly one public Python docstring correction."""
import ast
import copy
import json

import stateful_acceptance_common as c

ROOT, OUT, PYTHON = c.ROOT, c.OUT, c.PYTHON
read, sha, write = c.read, c.sha, c.write
DOCUMENTED_ASSET = 'python/src/shardloom/query.py'


def checked_runtime():
    snapshot = read(OUT / 'stateful-source-1.json')
    build = read(OUT / 'stateful-acceptance-build-1.json')
    actual = c.source_hashes()
    assert set(actual) == set(snapshot['source_hashes'])
    changed = sorted(name for name in actual if actual[name] != snapshot['source_hashes'][name])
    assert changed == [DOCUMENTED_ASSET], changed
    original = c.git('show', snapshot['head'] + ':' + DOCUMENTED_ASSET)
    current = (ROOT / DOCUMENTED_ASSET).read_text()
    old_tree, new_tree = ast.parse(original), ast.parse(current)
    old_fn, = [item for item in old_tree.body if isinstance(item, ast.FunctionDef) and item.name == 'from_batches']
    new_fn, = [item for item in new_tree.body if isinstance(item, ast.FunctionDef) and item.name == 'from_batches']
    assert isinstance(old_fn.body[0], ast.Expr) and isinstance(old_fn.body[0].value, ast.Constant)
    assert isinstance(new_fn.body[0], ast.Expr) and isinstance(new_fn.body[0].value, ast.Constant)
    before, after = old_fn.body[0].value.value, new_fn.body[0].value.value
    assert isinstance(before, str) and isinstance(after, str) and before != after
    assert 'pure filters/projections' in before
    assert all(text in after for text in ('sorting', 'aggregation', 'limits', 'drain'))
    old_fn.body[0] = copy.deepcopy(new_fn.body[0])
    assert ast.dump(old_tree, include_attributes=False) == ast.dump(new_tree, include_attributes=False)
    assert build['source_identity_sha256'] == snapshot['source_identity_sha256']
    assert sha(build['binary']) == build['binary_sha256']
    annotation = {'accepted_runtime_commit': snapshot['head'],
        'accepted_source_identity_sha256': snapshot['source_identity_sha256'],
        'assets_byte_identical': len(actual) - 1, 'asset_count_unchanged': len(actual),
        'docstring_only_asset': DOCUMENTED_ASSET,
        'accepted_file_sha256': snapshot['source_hashes'][DOCUMENTED_ASSET],
        'current_file_sha256': actual[DOCUMENTED_ASSET], 'function': 'from_batches',
        'prior_docstring': before, 'current_docstring': after,
        'entire_module_ast_identical_after_replacing_only_named_docstring': True,
        'executable_behavior_changed': False, 'binary_sha256': build['binary_sha256']}
    return snapshot, build, annotation


def portable(value):
    text = json.dumps(value, indent=2, allow_nan=False)
    for original, replacement in ((str(ROOT), '<repo>'), (str(OUT), '<stateful-uat>'), (str(ROOT.home()), '<home>')):
        text = text.replace(original, replacement)
    return text + '\n'
